chunks: Al-Nadr narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him) said, 'I will surely worship Allah today with such a worship, and will recite such a lovely recital, the likes of which I have never done before.' So he entered his prayer niche and did so. When he had completed his prayer, he [suddenly] saw a frog in the prayer niche. It said to him, 'O Dawud, are you pleased with yourself today due to your worship and recitation?' 'Yes,' he replied. It said, 'Do not be pleased [or impressed] by it, for verily I glorify Allah every night one thousand times, and with each glorification of mine three thousand praises branch out. And [at times] when I am in the depths of the water and a bird makes a sound in the air, I assume that it might be hungry so I come up to the surface of the water in order for it to eat me, while having committed no sin [to deserve that].'

key_terms.مِحْرَابُ: Prayer niche or place of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Prophet Dawud and the frog regarding humility and showing off?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Prophet Dawud’s momentary pride in his superior worship is humbled by a frog, which illustrates the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) over mere quantity of acts. The frog’s voluntary submission to birds, despite its innocence, serves as a profound counterpoint to human ego, reminding believers that true humility lies in recognizing one's dependence on God rather than self-congratulation.
